- code-explainer: Build a rich, interactive HTML explainer for a code change, feature, module, or whole system, with background, intuition, code walkthrough, diagrams, and a self-test quiz. Trigger when Phillip says "explain this diff/change/PR/branch", "code-explainer", "make me an explainer", "how does this system work", or after finishing development work he wants to actually understand. For redacted code it can also produce a team edition: successor-ready system docs committed to the repo and published to the Support space in Confluence ("document this for the team", "publish this to Confluence"). Every explainer also ships as an EPUB auto-sent to Phillip's own Kindle (standing authorization 2026-07-22; say "no kindle" to skip). Adapted from Geoffrey Litt's explain-diff prompt for a smart beginner retraining as an AI engineer.
- dj-backup: On-demand backup of the EP DJ Library volume (/Volumes/EP_DJ_Library) to Google Drive using rclone. Manual only — nothing syncs in the background. Stores a plain 1:1 mirror plus a dated archive of changed files and a snapshot of the rekordbox database, so recovery after a drive crash is a single command. Trigger when Phillip says "back up my DJ library", "run dj-backup", "back up the library to Google Drive", "what would a backup change", or asks to restore the library after a drive failure.
- dj-core: Orientation and routing for the DJ skill system — the shared invariants and the table that says which dj-* skill handles which request. Load when Phillip asks "what DJ skills do I have", "which skill handles X", "how is my DJ system organized", "route this DJ request", or when a DJ request is genuinely ambiguous between skills. Never fires on concrete workflow asks (URLs, label names, sync/backup/maintenance requests) — those route directly to their skill per the table inside.
- dj-favorites: Bidirectionally sync the tracks Phillip hearts on Tidal with his rekordbox pink favorites. Forward: Tidal hearts he already owns get a pink color, a "Favorite" My Tag, and Favorites playlist membership written into the live master.db via pyrekordbox (rekordbox closed; WAL-aware snapshot and dry run first). Hearts he does not own go into quarterly private Tidal placeholder playlists ("Favorites 2026-Q2") and are then downloaded into the library every run (all un-consumed quarters), producing an importable *_favorites.xml; --no-acquire skips that. Reverse: a track he colors pink in rekordbox gets hearted on Tidal in the same sweep (add-only, ISRC-matched, never un-hearts or un-pins; disable with --no-heartback). Re-runnable and idempotent. Trigger when Phillip says "sync my Tidal hearts", "update my favorites", "pull my favorited tracks", "run dj-favorites", "sync my pink tracks to Tidal", or asks to surface his hearted tracks in the DJ library, while working in /redacted/path
- dj-label-batch: Everything that takes record LABELS into the library — the favorite-labels registry and its three modes. (1) SWEEP the registry ("run the label batch", "sweep my favorite labels", "download the rest of my labels") — one combined review, one importable *_labeled.xml, every album web-verified. (2) SINGLE LABEL ("import the <label> catalog", "bring <label> into my library", "download and add the whole <label>", "pull the most recent tracks from [label]", "add [label] to my favorites and pull it" — formerly dj-label-import) via run --only, building the "Record Labels / <Label> / <Label> <year>" rekordbox tree. (3) HARVEST a Tidal playlist URL for the record labels behind its tracks ("surface the labels", "get the record labels for this playlist", "save the labels from this playlist", "add these labels to my favorites", "playlist labels" — formerly dj-playlist-labels); harvesting imports nothing. Tidal-folder-only builds (no library import) are dj-label-playlists; hearted tracks are dj-favorites.
- dj-label-playlists: Build a Tidal FOLDER for an entire record label — one "<Label>" folder holding one "<Label> <year>" playlist per release year (artists not split). Builds playlists on Tidal and IMPORTS NOTHING into rekordbox (importing a label is dj-label-batch; harvesting labels FROM a playlist is also dj-label-batch, not this). Discovers the catalog (artist-crawl + Discogs-style spine, copyright-verified), dedupes version-aware, drops continuous DJ-mix versions, shows a read-only plan, and writes to Tidal only on an explicit go. Trigger when Phillip names a record label and wants its releases AS TIDAL PLAYLISTS: "add everything on the label to playlists", "build playlists for the <label> label", "find all the <label> tracks on Tidal", "make a folder of <label> releases by year".
- dj-maintenance: Rekordbox library housekeeping, routine and occasional — sort INBOX tracks into BY GENRE + ENERGY ("sort my inbox", "run sort_inbox", "sweep unsorted"), audit unplaced tracks and duplicates ("audit my genre playlists"), zero-pad Camelot keys library-wide ("pad camelot keys" — a fresh-analyzed folder pads via dj-pipeline's pad stage instead), repair filenames rekordbox rejected on import ("fix the rejected filenames", "run path repair"), re-tag the Electronica bucket into specific genres ("retag electronica", "clean up the Electronica folder" — formerly dj-cleanup), scan playlists for streamed-from-Tidal entries ("scan playlists for streamed tracks"), and the INBOX rotation report ("rotate my inbox", "clean up my inbox", "dj-inbox-rotation" — dated intake > 30 days to drag to Old, Old > 90 days to delete; read-only, Phillip drags in rekordbox). Operates on a Fresh Export and produces a new XML to re-import; never part of an active set ingest (that's dj-pipeline).
- dj-master-set: Master a live DJ set recording (Pioneer XDJ-RX3 or any WAV/AIFF/FLAC). Evens out master-knob level drift that happened mid-recording, normalizes to a consistent loudness with a true-peak ceiling and preserved dynamic range, and encodes to lossless 24-bit FLAC that is smaller than the source WAV. The source is never modified and is archived first. Trigger when Phillip shares a DJ set/mix recording and asks to master it, level it, normalize it, even out the volume, "make it ready for playback", or shrink/convert it to FLAC.
- dj-pipeline: Get music INTO the rekordbox library (or just identify it) from any set-shaped input. Trigger on these input shapes — (1) an audio/set URL (SoundCloud, Mixcloud, anything yt-dlp-able) or a list of them ("process this mix", "track ID this", batch imports); (2) a Tidal playlist URL TO IMPORT ITS TRACKS ("import this Tidal playlist" — harvesting labels from a playlist is dj-label-batch instead); (3) a tracklist screenshot or typed artist–title list ("import this set", "get these tracks", "build a playlist from this tracklist", a 1001tracklists set — formerly dj-tracklist-intake); (4) ONE audio file already on disk ("add this track", "import this one file", "get this bootleg into my library", "ingest this WAV" — formerly dj-single-track-add); (5) identification only, no download ("what's in this mix", "ID this set, don't download", "just give me a tracklist" — formerly dj-setid). Whole folders needing tags only (no import) are dj-tagging; whole record labels are dj-label-batch.
- dj-set-builder: Build a short DJ set or transition around an anchor track using a tested, library-grounded engine. Finds owned tracks that are harmonically (Camelot) and energetically compatible with the anchor and sequences them before and after it, ranked on the library's own analyzed data (key, BPM, genre, energy, vocals). Deterministic and fast, no web calls by default. Trigger when Phil says "build a set around", "what plays before/after [track]", "find me tracks to mix into [track]", "closing set ending on [track]", or names a track and asks for compatible picks from his own library.
- dj-sync: The one ORCHESTRATOR — run everything new from Tidal into rekordbox as ONE command with ONE review gate: favorite-label releases, un-swept Tidal playlists, hearted favorites, then unattended execution to one combined *_synced.xml. Trigger when Phillip says "run a sync", "sync my library", "bring rekordbox current with Tidal", "dj-sync", "catch up my library". Single-purpose asks route to the workflow skills instead: just hearts → dj-favorites; just labels → dj-label-batch; one set/playlist → dj-pipeline; housekeeping only → dj-maintenance.
- dj-tagging: Tag a folder of newly-downloaded audio files with genre + album art via Beatport (Traxsource/Bandcamp fallback). Embeds CDJ-compatible 800x800 baseline JPEG art into FLAC, AIFF, WAV, and MP3 files. Patches tidal-dl-ng's broken FLAC PICTURE blocks. Trigger when Phillip says "tag these tracks", "run the tagger on this folder", "tag my Bandcamp downloads", "fix the album art on these files", or otherwise asks to tag a folder outside the URL-to-library pipeline.
- dj-vocal: Run vocal detection over the DJ library — score tracks for vocal prominence, tag with-vox + singer gender, and route vocal tracks into a "with vox" sub-playlist under each genre. Covers first-time setup (calibrate the threshold, create the empty playlists, restamp the back catalog) and ongoing re-runs. New tracks are scored automatically at ingest, so this skill is for the library-wide passes. Trigger when Phillip says "tag vocals", "run vocal detection", "find vocal tracks", "with vox", "restamp vocals", "dj-vocal", "calibrate vocals", or asks to surface vocal tracks in the library.
- meeting-summary: Process a Microsoft Teams .vtt meeting transcript into a paste-ready summary with action items and propagate durable insights into Phillip's workspace context files. Trigger when Phillip shares a .vtt file path, asks to "summarize this meeting", "process this transcript", or "wrap up [meeting name]". Default to internal Teams-chat output; switch to external email draft when Phillip says "external", "for the customer", or "for the partner".
- rescue: One-command backup and resurrection of Phil's entire PhilAI world (all repos, Documents siblings, secrets, and the Claude operator layer) via git remotes plus rclone to Google Drive. Trigger when Phil says "run a rescue backup", "rescue status", "back up everything", "back up my machine", or asks how to restore after a crash or onto a new machine. The DJ library volume is separate and belongs to dj-backup.
- retro: Run a structured retrospective with Phillip to review what went well, what missed, and what to change. Ask one question at a time, synthesize answers into concrete memory and skill updates. Trigger when Phillip says "retro", "retrospective", "let's review", or "how are we doing". Also prompt Phillip automatically in the Tuesday daily review and after any high-stakes ticket closes.

- compound-engineering:ce-explain: Create a durable visual teaching artifact for something worth learning. Use when the user wants to be taught, wants a deep explainer, wants to understand a substantial change, or wants a work recap built for retention. Not for ordinary Q&A, operational diagnosis, or a concise trade-off that belongs in chat. For learning, not repo docs or verdicts.
- compound-engineering:ce-handoff: Create a session handoff for another agent, or resume, find, and read any user-selected continuity source. Use when work or conversation must continue without access to the current session history.
- compound-engineering:ce-ideate: Generate and evaluate grounded ideas. Use when the user wants ideas, improvements, or surprising directions before choosing one to develop. Not for refining an idea they already have (ce-brainstorm) or judging one already on the table (ce-pov).
- compound-engineering:ce-optimize: Run metric-driven optimization loops. Use when improving a measurable outcome through experiments.
- compound-engineering:ce-plan: Create structured plans for multi-step work, including software and non-software tasks. Use when asked to plan, break down implementation, plan from requirements, or deepen an existing plan; prefer ce-brainstorm for exploratory framing.
- compound-engineering:ce-pov: Give a decisive, project-grounded point of view: a graded verdict on an external-adoption question, a holistic take on a document, or a position on a supplied approach set. Use for a solo POV. Use when asked to consult other models, reconcile their opinions, or `oracle`. Not for findings review (use ce-doc-review), neutral explainers, or generating options (use ce-ideate or ce-brainstorm).
- compound-engineering:ce-proof: Publish, read, comment on, or edit markdown in Proof. Use for Proof links, sharing specs/plans/drafts, or publish handoffs from planning workflows; avoid proofread, math, evidence, or proof-of-concept meanings.
- compound-engineering:ce-prototype: Build a throwaway prototype to answer how something should work, feel, or read. Use when committing the wrong answer would be expensive to unravel and a cheap sketch cannot settle it. Not a rough visual probe during brainstorming, not for deciding what to build, not polishing a feature that already works, not implementing the real thing.
- compound-engineering:ce-resolve-pr-feedback: Resolve PR review feedback. Use when addressing feedback already left on a PR. Not for reviewing the code before feedback exists; that is ce-code-review.
- compound-engineering:ce-riffrec-feedback-analysis: Analyze recorded product feedback into evidence for bugs and requirements. Use when a Riffrec capture or other screen, voice, or notes artifact needs interpretation. Use for Riffrec setup, capture, or sharing help when no recording exists yet.

- compound-engineering:ce-worktree: Set up isolated git worktrees — create a new branch for fresh work, or attach a worktree to an existing branch, PR, or commit. Use when starting isolated work or isolating an existing ref.
- compound-engineering:lfg: Run the full autonomous shipping pipeline end-to-end, hands-off with no check-ins. Use only when the user explicitly asks to build or ship something autonomously all the way to an open PR, or invokes lfg directly — it pushes and opens a PR without stopping. Not for in-the-loop work where the user reviews each step: use ce-plan, ce-work, ce-debug, or ce-commit-push-pr instead.
- frontend-design:frontend-design: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
